segments.t: Configure terminal display colors including text, background, cursor, selection, and the 16-color ANSI palette. Open via KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → ColorsKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.
Theme names (e.g., GitHub Dark, Dracula, etc.)

KTPH000Color ProfileKTPH001 allows you to select a preset theme that applies foreground, background, cursor, and cursor shape settings at once. Switching profiles will update the individual color controls. If KTPH002Apply ProfileKTPH003 is available, it will reset colors to the selected theme's defaults.

KTPH004Cursor blinksKTPH005 is your own preference and is kept when you switch color profiles: a profile contributes the cursor KTPH006shapeKTPH007 (block, underline, vertical bar), while the blinking on/off state stays as you set it. The terminal reads the flag as part of KTPH000 (for example KTPH001 when blinking is off), but your choice is stored separately as KTPH002 and wins over whatever style a profile, a theme or a per-connection setting carries — so switching profiles cannot turn blinking back on, and the setting survives restarts. A settings file written before that field existed keeps working: the choice is then read out of the stored KTPH003.

The KTPH000NormalKTPH001 and KTPH002BrightKTPH003 color palettes define the 16 ANSI colors (0–7 normal, 8–15 bright) used when KTPH004Enable terminal colorsKTPH005 is on. Each set of 8 colors corresponds to black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, and white. When terminal colors are disabled, only the configured KTPH006Text ColorKTPH007 and KTPH008BackgroundKTPH009 are used, ignoring all ANSI and TrueColor sequences.
